cards.title: My body belongs to me: Safe touch and the Swimsuit Rule
facts: Your body belongs exclusively to you; nobody has the right to touch you in a way that makes you feel uneasy.
The areas covered by a traditional swimsuit (chest, between legs, and bottom) are private parts.
do: Remember: Private parts are private; nobody should touch them except doctors or parents keeping you clean/healthy
Say a loud, firm 'NO!' if anyone tries to touch your private parts or asks you to touch theirs
Get away immediately and tell a trusted adult on your safety list right away
dont: Never keep unsafe touch a secret, even if the person tells you it's a game
Never feel guilty or blame yourself; you did nothing wrong

myths.statement: If someone you know well touches you uncomfortably, you must stay quiet because they are an adult.
myths.truth: Rules of safe touch apply to everyone: strangers, relatives, neighbors, and teachers alike. Speak up.

quiz.q: What are private parts on your body according to the universal Swimsuit Rule?
options: Parts covered by a swimsuit: chest, between legs, and bottom
quiz.explanation: Swimsuit areas are strictly private. Nobody should touch them inappropriately.

situations: At {at}, an adult makes {name} feel uneasy and uncomfortable by trying to touch under clothing.
scenario.question: What must {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Say 'NO!' loudly and firmly and move away immediately
rubric.note: Asserts clear bodily boundaries without hesitation.

rubric.point: Go straight to a trusted adult on your safety list and tell them everything
rubric.note: Breaks silence and secures immediate protection.

rubric.point: Remember that this is NEVER your fault and you have nothing to feel ashamed of
rubric.keys: not your fault|no shame|body belongs to you

cards.title: Secrets vs surprises: Good surprises vs unsafe secrets
facts: A good surprise (like a birthday gift or party) is temporary, happy, and will soon be shared openly with everyone.
An unsafe secret makes you feel worried, guilty, or scared in your tummy, and someone tells you never to tell parents.
do: Tell a trusted adult immediately if someone says: 'Keep this a secret from your parents'
Know the difference: Surprises bring happy smiles; unsafe secrets feel heavy and scary
Remember: No safe adult will ever ask a child to keep secrets from their mother or father
dont: Never promise to keep a secret that makes you feel uneasy or uncomfortable
Never keep a secret about someone touching you or showing inappropriate pictures

myths.statement: Keeping a secret that makes you feel scared is fine if an adult tells you you will get a reward.
myths.truth: Adults who ask children to keep secrets from parents are crossing safety boundaries. Always tell parents.

quiz.q: How can you tell the difference between a good surprise and an unsafe secret?
options: Surprises are temporary, happy, and shared soon; unsafe secrets make you feel scared and tell you to hide from parents
quiz.explanation: Safe surprises end in open happy celebrations; unsafe secrets cause fear and isolation.

situations: At {at}, an older acquaintance gives {name} an expensive gift and says: 'This is our special secret, don't tell your parents.'
scenario.question: How should {name} respond?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recognize that safe adults do not ask children to keep secrets from parents
Tell parents or a trusted adult about the gift and the secret request immediately
Understand that you will not get into trouble for reporting an unsafe secret

cards.title: My 5 Trusted Adults: Building your safety circle
facts: A 'Trusted Adult' is someone who listens carefully, believes you, respects boundaries, and takes action to protect you.
Having a pre-identified list of 5 trusted adults ensures you always know whom to turn to in distress.
do: Identify 5 adults you feel safe with (e.g. Mother, Father, School Counselor, Grandmother, Aunt, Favorite Teacher)
Make sure at least one of your 5 trusted adults is outside your immediate home (like a teacher or doctor)
If the first adult on your list does not listen or seems busy, go to the second adult immediately
dont: Never keep worries locked inside just because one adult didn't understand the first time
Never choose a trusted adult who makes you feel uncomfortable or tells you to hide things

myths.statement: If you tell one adult about a problem and they don't help, you must give up and suffer silently.
myths.truth: Adults can be distracted. Keep telling the next trusted adult on your list until someone takes action.

quiz.q: What is the most important quality of a 'Trusted Adult' on your safety list?
options: They give you lots of candy
They listen without judging, believe you, make you feel safe, and help solve problems
quiz.explanation: Trusted adults provide emotional security, objective guidance, and active protection.

situations: {name} is creating their personal 'Safety Hand' (5 Trusted Adults list) at {at}.
scenario.question: How should {name} select their trusted adults?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Choose 5 adults who listen patiently, believe you, and respect your feelings
rubric.note: Builds a reliable, empathetic safety network.

rubric.point: Include at least one person from school or community (like a favorite teacher or counselor)
Remember to keep telling the next adult on your list until someone listens and helps

dangerous: pick someone who tells you to keep secrets

cards.title: The stranger at the school gate: Lifts, candies and pets
facts: Tricking children with puppies, candy, or claiming 'Your mother sent me to pick you up' is a classic lure.
Parents will ALWAYS inform school authorities or provide the pre-agreed family Safe Word if someone else picks you up.
do: Step back at least 5 big steps (two arm-lengths) away from unfamiliar cars or strangers calling to you
Say firmly: 'No thank you, I will wait with my teacher inside the school gate'
Walk straight back into the school building and inform the security guard, principal, or teacher
dont: Never accept lifts, snacks, chocolates, or money from unfamiliar adults
Never get into a car or auto with someone unless your parents personally verified it with you

myths.statement: If a stranger at the school gate knows your nickname, that means your parents sent them to take you home.
myths.truth: Strangers can easily overhear your friends calling your name or read your school bag tag. Never go with them.

quiz.q: An unfamiliar person in a car outside school says: 'Your mother is unwell, hop in quickly so I can take you to her.' What do you do?
options: Do NOT get in; run back inside the school gate and tell the teacher or security guard immediately
quiz.explanation: Never enter an unfamiliar car. Always verify through school teachers and direct phone contact with parents.

situations: Waiting outside school at {at}, an unfamiliar adult approaches {name}: 'Your dad asked me to pick you up today, come with me.'
scenario.question: What is the only safe protocol for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do NOT go with the stranger and step back away from their vehicle
rubric.note: Avoids abduction and physical grab range.
rubric.keys: do not go|step back|refuse lift|stay away

rubric.point: Ask for the pre-agreed secret family 'Safe Word' or go back inside school to verify
Stay inside the school gate with teachers or security guards until parents arrive
rubric.keys: stay inside school|security guard|wait with teacher

sources.name: Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights (DCPCR)

cards.title: Feeling followed on the street: Crossing, shops and shouting
facts: Walking with confident posture, head held high, and scanning surroundings discourages opportunistic stalkers.
Heading into a brightly lit public shop or family-filled store instantly eliminates solitary vulnerability.
do: Cross the road deliberately to see if the person crosses too, confirming your suspicion
Do not go home to an empty house; walk immediately into a busy, well-lit public store, bank, or restaurant
Approach the shopkeeper or security guard clearly: 'I think I am being followed, please help me call my parents'
dont: Never walk into empty alleys, dark shortcuts, or deserted park pathways when feeling followed
Never hesitate to shout loudly: 'STOP! Leave me alone!' if someone approaches too closely

myths.statement: If someone is following you, walking into a dark quiet shortcut helps you sneak away faster.
myths.truth: Dark deserted alleys trap you without bystanders. Always head toward busy, well-lit crowds and shops.

quiz.q: What should you do immediately if you realize a stranger on foot or on a scooter is following you?
options: Walk into a dark empty alley
Head straight into a busy open shop, pharmacy, or bank with staff and call parents
quiz.explanation: Entering a public business provides immediate adult witnesses, CCTV coverage, and telephone access.

situations: Walking back from tuition at {at}, {name} notices an unfamiliar person matching their pace for three blocks.
scenario.question: What proactive safety moves should {name} make?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Cross to the other side of the road to confirm if they are tracking your path
Walk directly into the nearest busy shop, medical store, or family restaurant
rubric.note: Places yourself in a safe, populated, well-lit environment.

rubric.point: Ask the shopkeeper to help you call your parents or dial police 112
rubric.note: Activates immediate community and police protection.

sources.name: National Commission for Women (NCW Safety Guidelines)

cards.title: Home alone safety: Locked doors and phone rules
facts: Doors must remain deadbolted from the inside when staying home alone.
Telling callers or strangers at the door 'I am home alone' advertises vulnerability.
do: Keep the main entrance door and security latch firmly locked at all times
Look through the door peephole or window before responding to any doorbell
If a delivery or repairperson arrives, tell them through the closed door: 'My parents are busy, please leave the package outside'
dont: Never open the door to delivery partners, salespeople, or unfamiliar technicians when home alone
Never tell telephone callers or post on social media: 'Home alone today!'

myths.statement: If a delivery person brings a parcel for your parents while you are home alone, opening the door wide is polite.
myths.truth: Never open the door to anyone when home alone. Ask them to leave the parcel outside or return later.

quiz.q: What should you say through a locked door if a delivery person knocks while you are home alone?
options: I am home alone, come in
My parents are busy right now; please leave the parcel at the door or come back later
quiz.explanation: Saying 'parents are busy' signals adult presence in the house without opening the lock.

situations: Staying home alone for an hour at {at}, the doorbell rings and an unfamiliar courier asks {name} to open the door.
scenario.question: How should {name} manage this safely?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Keep the door firmly locked and do NOT open it
rubric.keys: keep door locked|do not open|stay locked

rubric.point: Speak through the closed door: 'My parents are busy, please leave the parcel outside'
rubric.note: Gives impression of adult presence indoors.
rubric.keys: parents are busy|leave outside|come back later

rubric.point: Call or text parents to inform them about the delivery knock
rubric.note: Keeps parents informed in real time.

dangerous: say nobody is home but me

sources.name: Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPRD Home Safety)

cards.title: Family secret Safe Word: The verification code
facts: A family 'Safe Word' is a secret code known exclusively to you and your parents.
If an emergency occurs and parents must send someone else to collect you, that person MUST know the Safe Word.
do: Choose a fun, memorable family secret word (e.g. 'BlueMango' or 'FlyingPanda') that you never share with friends
If an adult approaches saying 'Your parents sent me', demand: 'What is our family Safe Word?'
If the person cannot state the exact Safe Word, refuse to move and run to school teachers or security
dont: Never tell your family Safe Word to classmates, neighbours, or on social media
Never accept any explanation ('Your parents forgot to tell me the word') as an excuse

myths.statement: A family safe word should be an easy word like your pet's name that everyone in school knows.
myths.truth: The safe word must be a private, unique family secret that no outsider could ever guess.

quiz.q: What must an adult sent by your parents say before you agree to go with them in an emergency?
options: They must state your secret family 'Safe Word' accurately
quiz.explanation: The Safe Word proves direct, verified parental authorization.

situations: At {at}, an acquaintance approaches {name} saying: 'Your mother asked me to pick you up, hurry.'
scenario.question: What verification question must {name} ask?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Ask: 'What is our family secret Safe Word?'
rubric.keys: safe word|what is the safe word|secret code

rubric.point: If they do not know the exact word, refuse to go and step away immediately
rubric.keys: refuse to go|step away|do not leave

rubric.point: Notify school authorities or call parents directly to verify

dangerous: tell them the safe word yourself

sources.name: National Center for Missing and Exploited Children Safety Rules

cards.title: Lost in a crowded market or festival: Safe helpers
facts: Crowded fairs, railway stations, and melas can separate children from parents in seconds.
Wandering around searching in panic increases distance; finding designated uniform helpers is safest.
do: Stop walking immediately—stay near where you last saw family ('Freeze and stay in a safe spot')
Look for Safe Helpers: police officers, railway ticket examiners, security guards, or a mother with children
Recite your parents' mobile phone numbers clearly to the official helper and ask them to announce over public loudspeakers
dont: Never leave the building or festival ground with a stranger who offers to 'drive you home'
Never hide in dark corners or panic and wander into busy road traffic

myths.statement: If you get lost in a massive crowd, running around searching every stall is the best way to find parents.
myths.truth: Running makes you miss each other. Stay in one open, safe spot and approach a uniformed helper.

quiz.q: Who is the safest person to approach for help if you get lost in a shopping mall or crowded festival?
options: A stranger sitting in a car outside
A uniformed security guard, information desk executive, or a police officer
quiz.explanation: Uniformed personnel and customer help desks have public address loudspeaker systems to page parents.

situations: In a bustling festival fair at {at}, {name} turns around and realizes parents are nowhere in sight.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stop wandering and look for a uniformed police officer, security guard, or information counter
Provide parents' memorized mobile phone numbers clearly to the official helper
rubric.note: Enables direct phone contact with family.

rubric.point: Do not leave the festival venue with any stranger offering a private lift
rubric.keys: do not leave with stranger|stay in venue

dangerous: hide in dark alley and cry

sources.name: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)

cards.title: Spotting online grooming: Flattery, gifts and secrecy
facts: Online predators spend weeks building trust through excessive flattery, gaming gifts, and shared 'secrets'.
Grooming follows a pattern: isolating the young person from parents, requesting photos, and shifting to private apps.
do: Be on high alert if an online acquaintance showers you with gaming gifts (Robux, skins) or says: 'Only I understand you'
Recognize the red flag when an online friend insists: 'Don't tell your parents we chat' or asks to move to Snapchat/Discord DMs
Take screenshots, block the user, and show the conversation to a trusted adult immediately
dont: Never send private photos, video call strangers without clothing, or reveal personal school locations
Never agree to meet an online-only acquaintance in person in the physical world

myths.statement: An online friend from an overseas gaming group who sends you gifts and asks for personal photos is just being friendly.
myths.truth: Requesting personal photos or asking children to hide chats from parents is textbook predatory grooming.

quiz.q: What is a major red-flag sign of online grooming in gaming and social media chats?
options: Asking you to keep your chats a secret from parents and asking for private photos
quiz.explanation: Demands for secrecy and requests for personal photos indicate malicious predatory behavior.

situations: An older gamer in an online community at {at} sends {name} gifts and texts: 'You are so special, don't tell your parents we chat, send me a private photo.'
scenario.question: What is the urgent safety response for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recognize this immediately as predatory online grooming and do NOT send any photos
Block the user immediately and preserve screenshots of the messages
rubric.note: Captures forensic evidence while cutting contact.

rubric.point: Show the conversation to parents or report on Childline 1098 / cybercrime portal

dangerous: agree to meet in person alone

cards.title: Handling uncomfortable comments: Saying NO and telling
facts: You have the constitutional and moral right to bodily integrity, personal dignity, and emotional respect.
Uncomfortable comments about your body or personal space from anyone (peers or adults) are unacceptable.
do: Use a firm, loud voice with eye contact: 'Stop! I do not like that comment, do not say that to me'
Walk away with your head held high to a populated, safe area
Report the incident to a parent, teacher, or trusted adult: remember that telling is NOT 'snitching'
dont: Never laugh along or smile nervously when someone makes an inappropriate comment about your body
Never keep uncomfortable encounters bottled up inside

myths.statement: If an adult makes an uncomfortable remark about your body, you must smile and stay quiet to be polite.
myths.truth: Politeness never requires tolerating boundary violations. You have the right to assert boundaries firmly.

quiz.q: What is the difference between 'snitching' and 'reporting' an uncomfortable safety incident?
options: Snitching is trying to get someone in petty trouble; reporting is protecting yourself or others from harm
quiz.explanation: Reporting safety violations is an act of courage that protects the entire community.

situations: At {at}, an older person makes an inappropriate, creepy comment about {name}'s appearance that feels deeply wrong.
scenario.question: How should {name} react?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Say firmly: 'Stop, do not speak to me like that' and walk away immediately
rubric.keys: say stop|firm boundary|walk away|don'?t speak like that

rubric.point: Tell a trusted adult, parent, or school counselor what happened right away
Understand that you have the right to feel safe and respected at all times
rubric.keys: right to respect|feel safe|not your fault

dangerous: stay silent and cry in room

sources.name: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights

cards.title: Dealing with school bullying: Adults have a duty to act
facts: Bullying is repetitive, aggressive behavior involving an imbalance of power (physical, verbal, or social).
Under CBSE and state school education rules, schools are legally mandated to have Anti-Bullying Committees.
do: Tell the bully firmly once: 'Stop, leave me alone' in a calm, confident voice, then walk away
Report every bullying incident to your class teacher, principal, school counselor, or parents with specific dates
Stay in groups of friendly classmates during recess, corridors, and bus rides (bullies target isolated students)
dont: Never believe the cruel insults bullies say about you (bullying reflects the bully's insecurity, not your worth)
Never resort to dangerous physical violence that can get you hurt or suspended

myths.statement: Being bullied in school is just a normal character-building ritual that every student must endure quietly.
myths.truth: Bullying causes severe psychological trauma and is strictly illegal under school safety regulations.

quiz.q: Under CBSE guidelines, what committee must every school maintain to protect students from harassment?
quiz.explanation: Schools are legally required to maintain anti-bullying committees to resolve harassment complaints.

situations: A group of students at {at} repeatedly pushes, insults, and steals {name}'s lunchbox during recess.
scenario.question: What is the constructive, empowered response for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Report the repeated bullying formally to the class teacher, school counselor, or principal
Confide in parents so they can write an official note to the school administration
rubric.note: Secures family backing and formal institutional records.

rubric.point: Remember that you are worthy, valued, and bullying is NEVER your fault

sources.name: CBSE School Safety and Anti-Bullying Directives

cards.title: Avoiding unsafe isolated spots: Stairwells, basements and abandoned areas
facts: Over 80% of peer bullying and predatory harassment occurs in unmonitored, isolated 'blind spots'.
Empty basements, deserted terraces, and isolated washrooms lack adult oversight and CCTV coverage.
do: Always use buddy pairs: take a trusted classmate along when visiting distant school washrooms or supply rooms
Stick to well-lit, populated corridors and active campus areas during recess and after-school hours
If you must walk through a quiet stairwell, walk purposefully with head up and stay observant
dont: Never hang out in dark, deserted school basements, abandoned sports sheds, or rooftop terraces
Never agree to follow an acquaintance into an empty, isolated room to 'see a secret'

myths.statement: Hanging out in dark abandoned campus buildings alone is completely safe if you are brave.
myths.truth: Isolated unmonitored zones lack emergency exits, witnesses, and immediate adult assistance.

quiz.q: What is the 'Buddy System' rule for visiting distant school areas like sports sheds or quiet washrooms?
options: Always take a trusted friend along so you are never isolated in unmonitored spaces
quiz.explanation: The buddy system ensures mutual safety, immediate assistance, and deterrence against harassment.

situations: During free period at {at}, an older student invites {name} to an empty, deserted basement storeroom.
scenario.question: How should {name} respond?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Politely refuse to enter isolated unmonitored areas and stay in public corridors
rubric.keys: refuse|stay in public|avoid isolated basement|stay in light

rubric.point: Recognize that isolated unmonitored spaces represent common safety risk zones
Use the buddy system and stick to active, populated areas of the campus

sources.name: National Institute of Public Cooperation and Child Development (NIPCCD)

cards.title: Saying NO to familiar adults: Bodily autonomy and consent
facts: Most child boundary violations are committed by people known to the child (relatives, tutors, neighbors).
Children are never obligated to endure uncomfortable physical affection (forced hugs, tickling, sitting on laps).
do: Understand that respect does not require surrendering your bodily comfort: a warm 'Namaste' or handshake is completely polite
Say firmly: 'I prefer not to hug right now, namaste!' if forced into uncomfortable physical contact
Tell your parents if a relative, neighbor, or tutor touches you in a way that feels awkward or wrong
dont: Never force yourself to sit on an adult's lap if it makes you feel uneasy
Never believe an adult who says: 'If you loved your uncle/tutor, you would let me touch you'

myths.statement: Children must always allow relatives and family friends to kiss and hug them even if they feel uncomfortable.
myths.truth: Bodily autonomy begins in childhood. You have the total right to choose respectful non-physical greetings.

quiz.q: What is a polite, culturally respectful alternative to an uncomfortable hug from a visiting relative?
options: A warm smile, folded hands 'Namaste', or a polite handshake
quiz.explanation: Namaste is an ancient, respectful Indian greeting that maintains healthy physical boundaries.

situations: At a family gathering at {at}, an adult relative insists {name} sit on their lap, which makes {name} feel uneasy.
scenario.question: How can {name} uphold their bodily boundaries respectfully?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Step back politely and say: 'I prefer to sit on this chair, namaste Uncle'
rubric.note: Asserts bodily comfort with poise and respect.
rubric.keys: sit on chair|prefer not to|namaste|step back

rubric.point: Remember that you have the complete right to decide who touches your body
Tell your parents privately if any relative's behavior continues to feel uncomfortable

sources.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development Guidelines

cards.title: Memorizing vital safety info: Phone numbers and home address
facts: Smartphones run out of battery, get lost, or break during real-world crises.
A child who has memorized two parental phone numbers can be safely reunited within 15 minutes.
do: Memorize your mother's and father's 10-digit mobile phone numbers by heart through daily rhythm practice
Know your full home address clearly: Flat/House number, building name, road, colony, and city
Know your school's full name and your blood group if possible
dont: Never rely 100% on phone contacts list without knowing numbers in your head
Never write your phone number and home address in large visible letters on the outside of your backpack

myths.statement: Memorizing phone numbers is obsolete in the 21st century because smartphones store everything.
myths.truth: If your phone battery dies or is lost, you are helpless unless parent numbers are memorized in your mind.

quiz.q: What two pieces of personal information should every student know by heart from memory?
options: Their high score in video games
At least two parental 10-digit phone numbers and their full home address
quiz.explanation: Parent phone numbers and home address are foundational life-saving safety coordinates.

situations: During a school trip at {at}, {name}'s mobile phone battery dies completely and {name} gets separated.
scenario.question: How does {name}'s mental preparation save the day?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recite mother's or father's 10-digit mobile number from memory to the police or station master
rubric.keys: recite phone number|memorized number|call mother|call father

rubric.point: State full home address, colony, and school name clearly
Approach a uniformed officer or customer help desk calmly

dangerous: panic because phone battery is dead
give up and wander into streets

sources.name: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights Guidelines

cards.title: Emergency helplines: Child Helpline 1098 and Police 112
facts: 1098 is India's 24/7, free, emergency phone outreach service for children in need of care and protection.
Calls to 1098 and 112 can be made from ANY landline or mobile phone even with zero balance and no SIM.
do: Dial 1098 if you or another child is facing abuse, child labor, child marriage, or extreme distress
Dial 112 for immediate all-in-one emergency response (Police, Fire, and Ambulance)
Speak clearly and state your city, location, and what emergency help you need
dont: Never make prank or prank joke calls to 1098 or 112 (it blocks lines for children in real danger)
Never fear that calling 1098 will get you into trouble; it is a safe child-friendly service

myths.statement: You need a mobile recharge and positive balance to call emergency helplines like 112 or 1098.
myths.truth: Emergency calls to 112 and 1098 are legally mandated to connect free of cost from all telecom networks.

quiz.q: What is the official nationwide emergency helpline number dedicated exclusively to children in India?
quiz.explanation: 1098 operates 24/7 across India under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

situations: A student at {at} learns that a classmate is being subjected to severe physical harm and needs help.
scenario.question: What confidential emergency action can be taken?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Call Child Helpline 1098 or Police 112 to report the situation safely
Provide the location, school, or residential details clearly to the counselor
Understand that calls to 1098 are confidential, free, and protected by law

dangerous: post on social media without reporting

sources.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development (Childline 1098)

cards.title: Supporting a friend who confides in you about an unsafe situation
facts: Children experiencing abuse or boundary violations often confide in a best friend before any adult.
A supportive peer listens without judgment, validates their pain, and helps connect them to safe adults.
do: Listen calmly, believe them completely, and say: 'Thank you for telling me, I believe you, it is not your fault'
Gently explain: 'I care about your safety too much to keep this secret. Let's talk to our school counselor together'
Go with them to hold their hand while speaking to a trusted teacher or parent
dont: Never promise to keep a secret that involves someone hurting your friend or them hurting themselves
Never judge, mock, or share your friend's sensitive secret with other classmates as gossip

myths.statement: If a friend tells you someone is hurting them at home, keeping their secret forever is true friendship loyalty.
myths.truth: True friendship protects lives. Harm and abuse must never be kept secret. Tell a trusted adult.

quiz.q: What is the most supportive thing to say when a friend confides that someone touched them inappropriately?
options: I believe you, it is NOT your fault, and I am here to help you get safe adult support
You must have done something wrong
quiz.explanation: Believing the victim and affirming zero blame relieves guilt and enables healing.

situations: During lunch break at {at}, a close classmate breaks down in tears and confides about an unsafe touch incident.
scenario.question: How should {name} support their friend?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Listen with deep empathy, believe them completely, and reassure: 'It is not your fault'
rubric.keys: i believe you|not your fault|listen with empathy

rubric.point: Encourage and accompany them to speak with the school counselor or trusted teacher
rubric.note: Bridges the child to professional protection.

rubric.point: Do not gossip or spread their confidential story across class group chats

dangerous: promise to keep abuse a secret forever

sources.name: NCPCR Guidelines on Peer Support in Child Protection

cards.title: Safe travel in cabs and autos: Live location and safety checks
facts: Traveling independently in app-based cabs or auto-rickshaws requires simple routine verification habits.
Live location sharing allows parents to track your vehicle's GPS route in real time on a digital map.
do: Verify the vehicle license plate, driver name, and car model against your app booking screen before getting in
Share your trip live location with your parents on WhatsApp or through the cab app's safety feature
Check that the rear interior door child-lock is not engaged, so you can open the door from the inside anytime
dont: Never board a cab or auto if the driver has an unauthorized stranger sitting in the front passenger seat
Never get into a cab whose license plate does not match the app details

myths.statement: It is rude to check the license plate number of a taxi before getting inside.
myths.truth: Verifying license plates against your booking screen is a basic, universal personal safety rule.

quiz.q: What safety feature on your smartphone should you activate when traveling alone in an auto or cab?
options: Share your 'Live Location' with your parents on WhatsApp or through the transit app
quiz.explanation: Live location sharing gives parents real-time GPS tracking of your vehicle's speed and route.

situations: {name} needs to take an auto-rickshaw or app cab home from tuition at {at}.
scenario.question: What safety routine should {name} follow?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Verify the vehicle license plate number against the booking screen before boarding
rubric.note: Guarantees you enter the authorized vehicle.

rubric.point: Share live trip location on WhatsApp with parents immediately upon starting the ride
Sit directly behind the driver (not in front) and ensure you can open the door from inside

dangerous: board vehicle with wrong number plate
accept ride with stranger in passenger seat

sources.name: MoRTH Guidelines for Passenger Safety in Commercial Transport

cards.title: Trusting your gut feeling: That uneasy knot in your stomach
facts: Your brain processes millions of subconscious sensory cues (body language, tone, micro-expressions) instantly.
An unexplained feeling of dread, goosebumps, or an uneasy knot in your stomach is your internal alarm bell.
do: Trust your instincts: If a person, place, or situation feels 'weird' or 'wrong', treat it as a valid danger signal
You do not need to justify or explain why you feel unsafe before removing yourself from a situation
Make an excuse ('My mom is calling me right now') and leave the room or area immediately
dont: Never ignore an intuitive warning feeling just to appear 'polite' or 'cool'
Never stay in a situation that makes your tummy turn just because everyone else is staying

myths.statement: A gut feeling of uneasiness is just silly childish imagination that should be ignored.
myths.truth: Intuition is your brain's evolved survival radar detecting subtle danger cues. Always honor your instincts.

quiz.q: What should you do if an unfamiliar situation or person gives you an intense uneasy feeling in your stomach?
options: Force yourself to stay and laugh
Trust your gut instinct, create an excuse, and leave for a safe place immediately
quiz.explanation: Honoring your intuition keeps you steps ahead of danger before a threat escalates.

rubric.point: Trust the uneasy instinct and prioritize personal safety without worrying about being polite
Make a calm, quick exit excuse ('I must head home now, my parent is waiting') and leave
rubric.keys: make excuse and leave|exit immediately|walk away

rubric.point: Rejoin trusted friends or parents in a well-lit, populated environment
